Since interaction denotes some type of mutuality or reciprocity, the true measure of economic interaction would take account of two-way traffic in employees, goods, and services. Variables E and F reflect the proportion of land in the proposed commercial zone area either zoned for or devoted to industrial or commercial uses. The highest cited statistic is 15 percent for Birmingham, Ala., and the preponderance of the remaining statistics indicate a very low percentage. There is no standard of comparison given, however, in order to evaluate these statistics with the percentage of land generally devoted to these purposes in suburban areas which have been deemed commercially integrated with a base municipality. Variable J indicates that there is a substantial sharing of public utilities by base municipalities and outlying areas.
